rationale: Narrows the trim child's open gap with a source reading of the leader's recorded-accepted bookkeeping, so that the remaining part of that question is only the storage-level entry point rather than the whole route. No execution was requested and nothing was run: reading LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx (util.rs 186-191) shows the bound is the minimum over an accepted_indexes vector that the source asserts is initialised for every node (its expect message is Should be all initialised to 0), and set_promise rewrites the promise entry for the sender on every promise. A node therefore has a recorded accepted index from the start, and trim can pass a live replica's accepted index only when that replica's own recorded value has itself been inflated by the re-synchronization drift. That closes, by source, the sub-route the gap named as a peer compacted while its recorded values were still truthful: the trim bound cannot exceed a truthful peer's accepted index, because the truthful peer's own record keeps the minimum honest. What remains of the gap is the storage-level entry point - a direct range read or a store-level trim below a compacted index, which the Storage trait leaves to the implementer and which no run exercised - and the answer records that split explicitly, keeping the gap unresolved while marking the in-cluster half closed. The account's conclusion, witness, controls and knowledge uses are unchanged, and the trimmed trim-bound fact now carries the initialisation evidence in its own conditions in the same update.

knowledge.statement: Trim's bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes and both trim paths respect it: with no explicit index that minimum is used, and an explicit index above it is refused with that same minimum reported. The bound can therefore exceed only the content of replicas whose recorded accepted index has itself drifted; a replica whose report is still truthful keeps the bound at or below its own accepted index, so no in-cluster re-synchronization request can fall below a compacted index that trim produced.
knowledge.conditions: Leader role, reached from the public trim() with None or Some(index). The minimum is taken over the leader's accepted_indexes vector, which the source asserts is initialised for every node (get_min_all_accepted_idx at util.rs 186-191 returns the vector's minimum and its expect message reads Should be all initialised to 0), and set_promise rewrites the entry for the promising node, so every configuration member has a recorded value even if it has never sent an Accepted message. Witnessed in receipt ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a (recorded values 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content, compacted 7, events 9-15). The unexecuted remainder is a storage or caller that asks the storage trait directly for a prefix below the compacted index, whose behaviour the trait leaves to the implementer.
knowledge.changed_premise: Adds the basis for the in-cluster half of the claim rather than leaving it as an inference from the drift: the minimum is taken over a per-node vector the source says is initialised for every member, so a truthful replica keeps the bound at or below its own accepted index and no re-synchronization request can fall below a trim-produced compacted index. Previously the statement asserted the same consequence from the observed drift alone.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed and bounded, with the second producer recorded and with the suffix route split into an executed in-cluster half and an unexecuted storage-level half. The trim witness stands: with recorded accepted indexes drifted to 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content and every node's decided report at 9, trim(None) returned no error and compacted index 7, past the leader's own content, after which its reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15). The discriminator this question carried asked whether a producer other than trim can raise a compacted index past a replica's content, and the snapshot receipt answers that it can: with the same drifted state, snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, advanced the leader's compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). That second producer is stricter in one respect and looser in another than trim: it needs no recorded accepted index at all - its bound is the leader's decided index - so a drift confined to the decided index would be enough for it, while trim additionally needs the drifted value to be the configuration's minimum recorded accepted index. What remains bounded from the earlier reading: both producers are bounded by values the leader derives for itself, so a replica whose recorded report is still truthful keeps trim's bound honest (the minimum), and the snapshot witness also required the leader's own decided index to have drifted. Correction review: the drift knowledge this account cites was narrowed to revision 2, which keeps the half this account needs - the reported accepted index drifts one further index per re-synchronization round, inflating exactly the recorded accepted indexes the trim bound is derived from - and bounds the decided index to the rounds in which a write quorum of drifted reports covers it; this account never assumes the decided index keeps following the drift, since it reads the decided values from its own receipt's samples (every node at 9), so the narrowing leaves its conclusion unchanged and the knowledge use is re-read at revision 2 below. The suffix route is now split by source and by execution. Executed in-cluster: in the snapshot-capable sibling case the lagging replica re-synchronized below the leader's compacted index (the leader had compacted to 8 with a snapshot holding zero ids) was not refused and did not panic - it received that complete snapshot and no suffix, reported accepted 10 / decided 10 and read two decided entries where the configuration decided six (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162). Closed by source: a re-synchronization request below a trim-produced compacted index cannot arise inside the cluster, because the trim bound is the minimum over the leader's accepted_indexes vector and that vector carries an entry for every configuration member from the start (get_min_all_accepted_idx at util.rs 186-191 returns the vector's minimum and its expect message reads Should be all initialised to 0, while set_promise rewrites the sender's entry on every promise). A replica that has never been inflated therefore keeps its own accepted index in the minimum and trim cannot pass it; only inflation of that replica's own recorded value moves the bound, which is what the witness shows. What is left of the gap is the storage-level entry point: a direct range read or a store-level trim below a compacted index, whose behaviour the Storage trait leaves to the implementer and which no execution exercised, and the abort that this lineage did produce comes from a different entry point, the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance (40ab66a5c5c847619ae2ff68b85641e7-question-1).

b26c13954e184cd2b9fdfda975aff136-gap-4.explanation: Split into a closed in-cluster half and an open storage-level half, so the gap stays unresolved. Closed by source and execution: a replica re-synchronizing below a compacted index does not panic - it is handed a complete snapshot built from the empty part of the log and a shortened decided log (receipt 0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162, guarded result event 162 with panicked false) - and a request below a trim-produced compacted index cannot arise inside the cluster at all, because the trim bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes and that per-node vector is initialised for every member (get_min_all_accepted_idx, util.rs 186-191, whose expect message reads Should be all initialised to 0), so a truthful replica keeps the bound at or below its own accepted index and only its own inflation can move it. Still open: the storage-level routes the gap names - a direct range read and a store-level trim below a compacted index - which the Storage trait leaves to the implementer and which no run exercised; and a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot arriving at a NoSnapshot instance, which cannot be produced inside a cluster whose nodes share one entry type because the sender panics first.

The conclusion, the witness and the content comparison are therefore unchanged; the knowledge use is re-read at revision 2.

knowledge.assertion: trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
trim's bound is the minimum over a per-node recorded accepted vector, so a truthful replica keeps it at or below its own accepted index
the reported accepted index drifts one index per re-synchronization round while the decided index follows only while a write quorum covers it
a replica re-synchronized below the compacted index receives a complete snapshot built from the empty range

counterevidence: Every node's decided report had also drifted to 9, so the documented all-decided precondition was satisfied only in the drifted bookkeeping; the obligation I rely on is that the compacted index must not exceed the entries the leader holds, which it did (7 for trim, 8 for the snapshot).
The trim call returned Ok, so nothing in its own result signals the over-compaction; the witness is the compacted index together with the content sampled before and after.

The in-cluster route below a compacted index is now executed rather than argued, and it does not abort: the lagging replica was re-synchronized with a complete but empty snapshot and a shortened decided log (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 161, 162), so the over-compaction of this account leads to a silent loss on a lagging replica; the abort seen in the same lineage belongs to the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance and is recorded under its own question.

The peer-side sub-route is closed by source rather than merely untested: a truthful replica's recorded accepted index stays in the minimum the trim bound is taken from, so the bound cannot pass such a replica and no request below the compacted index follows from it.
limitations: The trim over-compaction is bounded to replicas whose recorded accepted index has drifted; a truthful replica would have kept the bound lower, and the per-node initialisation of the recorded vector is the reason.

The underflow remainder is a property of a storage or caller that requests a prefix below the compacted index by a route other than the cluster's own log syncs: a direct range read and a store-level trim below a compacted index remain unexecuted, other storage implementations may differ, and the trait leaves out-of-range behaviour to the implementer. The abort observed in this lineage came from the NoSnapshot snapshot-call path, not from this remainder.
The baseline comparisons of both receipts are unknown because they were admitted through event names shared across cases in one execution; those states are asserted from the sampled operands.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one leader change for trim and one snapshot-capable entry type were exercised; the peers that receive a forwarded compaction were not sampled beyond their accepted and decided indexes, and the lagging-replica outcome was observed with the leader's log empty above its compacted index.

For the trim path the observed over-compaction is the minimum of the drifted recorded values, so the number of indices it passes beyond the leader's content depends on how many rounds each replica drifted; only one such combination was sampled.

The initialisation claim for the recorded accepted vector is read from the source's own expect message and from set_promise rewriting the sender's entry; no execution sampled the vector directly or ran a trim while one member had never promised.
